summary: Imperium: Classics is a card-driven civilization builder where you cycle a small deck (via the 'move through deck' mechanic) to unlock increasingly powerful cards while balancing expansion against unrest; each of the eight civilizations plays with genuinely different mechanics and priorities. It plays fast for its weight, works very well solo against a card-driven AI, and rewards efficient engine-building over direct conflict.
praised: Strong, well-tuned solo mode with a card-based AI opponent
Deep asymmetry — each civilization feels mechanically distinct, not just re-skinned
Fast turns and short deck-cycling create a satisfying rhythm without long downtime
criticised: Low direct player interaction — often feels like parallel solitaire at the table
Rulebook and icon-heavy cards have a steep initial learning curve
Some civilizations/cards are viewed as stronger or more fun than others (balance complaints)
Take-that elements exist but are minor, so conflict-seeking players may find it too dry

interaction.kind: mostly parallel empire-building with occasional take-that cards

scoring.why: Points come from your civilization's unique track, end-game card bonuses, and accumulated achievements, so the winner is decided by how efficiently you built your engine across several scoring channels rather than one dominant strategy.
